acceptance_criteria.description: The workspace resolves on Rust 1.93.1 and exposes only the coop-protocol member in this wave.
RegionId ordinals and conversions are explicit, tested, and independent of the engine Region enum.
TrainerInstanceId, BadgeId, FlyPointId, and EventId reject bare, lowercase, malformed, unknown-region, and cross-kind confusion while round-tripping canonical identities.
WorldLocation, WorldZone, RegionalProgress, and compatibility/version types use fixed-width fields and deterministic serialization.
Regional tier tests prove the supplied Hoenn/Kanto example and prove badges from other regions cannot influence the battle region.
Symmetric group and atomic travel tests prove denial preserves the group and source zone, while an all-entitled transfer succeeds.
Format, clippy with warnings denied, all workspace tests, and git diff checks pass.

closed_decisions: Use explicit independent wire ordinals UNSPECIFIED=0, HOENN=1, KANTO=2, JOHTO=3, and SEVII=4; never reuse engine enum ordinals.
Use strict canonical REGION:LOCAL_KEY identities with uppercase ASCII local keys and type-distinct wrappers for trainer instances, badges, fly points, and events.
WorldLocation contains region, u16 map_group, u16 map_number, i16 x, and i16 y; raw engine structs never cross the host protocol.
RegionalProgress contains one concrete region, u16 badge_mask, u32 story_checkpoint, and deterministic duplicate-free collections of same-region trainer and fly identities.
Group battle tier requires complete progress for the battle region and returns the minimum badge count in that region; missing progress fails closed and other-region badges are ignored.
Groups are symmetric sets of exactly two distinct character IDs with no leader, owner, or host field.
Cross-region group travel is atomic: any missing route entitlement denies the transfer without mutating the group or current world zone.
Use serde JSON contracts plus repr(u8) and explicit wire conversion methods; reject unknown protocol/schema versions and unknown region ordinals.
Keep dependencies minimal and forbid unsafe Rust.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit any PokéCrossroads C, assembly, map, save, battle, or build files.
Do not implement authentication, persistence, networking, server state, sidecar behavior, launcher UI, or ROM bridge behavior in this unit.
Do not stage, commit, switch branches, fetch, push, contact remotes, or mutate docs/orchestration.
Do not add a leader, host, or owner concept to groups.
Do not infer Sevii as Kanto in the shared protocol and do not assume Johto is currently playable.
Do not relax clippy warnings or add allow attributes merely to silence diagnostics.
objective: Implement and verify the minimal Rust workspace and region-safe shared protocol contract for PokéCrossroads cloud co-op.

return_when: All acceptance criteria are resolved and every required verification command has a recorded outcome.
A concrete blocker prevents further progress within the owned files and execution budget.
